text: Thirteen quick ones, a sentence or two each. Question ten. What are the three types of fact tables? Transaction: one row per event, like a deposit. Periodic snapshot: one row per entity per period, like a month-end balance. Accumulating snapshot: one row per process, like a loan application, updated in place as each milestone lands. Question eleven. When would you choose a periodic snapshot over a transaction fact? When the question is where things stood. Ben made no transaction in February, and his February balance, five hundred dollars, is still a row. Question twelve. What is a factless fact table? Keys and no measures: which products were on promotion in which store, each day. Count rows to answer it, but count what's asked. Store five promoted three products last week, in eleven rows. Question thirteen. What is a degenerate dimension? A key with no table behind it, like an order number on the order-line fact. It has nothing to describe, so it stays on the fact, and you still group by it. Question fourteen. What is a junk dimension? Small flags, is promo, is gift wrap and is expedited, gathered into one table of every combination: eight rows, and one key on the fact instead of three flags. Question fifteen. What is the purpose of a date dimension, and what columns does it typically include? One row per day, three hundred sixty-six for 2024, with year, quarter, month, week and weekend worked out once. The columns that matter most are the ones no function knows: holidays and the fiscal calendar. Question sixteen. What is a conformed dimension? One dimension shared by several facts, with the same keys and the same meanings, so their numbers line up.
